estimates.outcome: Design fixation score: features of the example repeated in each sketch (condition effect)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two HCI researchers with experience teaching and evaluating design counted example features in each sketch. DFS is the number of repeated features divided by the example’s 14 salient features. The fitted binomial model uses the feature count and a probit link. Raters were blind to the experiment’s aims; the paper does not explain whether their counts were combined before modelling. PDF pp. 4-5, Section 3.1; PDF p. 7, Section 3.4; PDF p. 8, Section 4.2.

regression.model: Bayesian binomial regression of repeated example features on Inspiration Stimulus, with a probit link and random intercepts for participant and image. Baseline is the reference condition. Posterior SD as printed: 0.13. This is posterior dispersion of the coefficient, not an outcome SD or a frequentist standard error.

estimates.notes: The structured coefficient and interval follow the table. These are Bayesian posterior means and compatibility intervals, not frequentist confidence intervals. ci_of difference refers to the condition coefficient on the stated model scale; raw means the outcome was not standardized, and the probit/log link has not been inverted. Parenthesized posterior SDs are retained literally in regression.model because the schema has no posterior-SD field; regression.se and all outcome SDs remain null. Where test is present, type other denotes the printed Bayes factor, not a t or F statistic. se_basis participant reflects the participant random effects for sketch-level models or the single response per participant for count models; it does not relabel posterior SD as a frequentist SE. No analysis-specific arm counts or two-arm output count are printed. Arm-level posterior predictions appear only in figures and were not digitized. Construct other follows the screening form: copying a supplied example is not recoded as across-person diversity. Higher values mean more fixation and less creativity. The results text gives a different upper compatibility bound from Table 1; the table is transcribed.

estimates.outcome: Variety: number of clusters covered by a participant’s sketches (total effects)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two raters blind to condition grouped sketches into 83 mutually exclusive clusters. The normalized score is (clusters covered by a participant minus one)/(total clusters minus one). The negative binomial model instead uses the number of clusters covered minus one, with a log link. The direct-effect model additionally adjusts for Fluency. This is variety within a participant, coded flexibility. PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, Equation 3; PDF p. 9, Section 4.4 and Table 3.

regression.model: Bayesian negative binomial regression of the number of clusters covered minus one on Inspiration Stimulus, with a log link. Total-effects specification without Fluency. Baseline is the reference condition. Posterior SD as printed: -.28. This is posterior dispersion of the coefficient, not an outcome SD or a frequentist standard error.

open_items: The experiment sample is printed, but no creativity model reports its analyzed participant N or arm-specific analyzed Ns. Equal allocation and sex-specific counts are printed; arm totals and two-arm totals would require arithmetic and are left null. No analyzed count was inferred from degrees of freedom, prompt totals, or absence of reported attrition.

No participant-level or output-level outcome SD, standardized effect, or numerical observed arm mean is printed. Arm posterior predictions and their standard-error bars are plotted without numeric labels. Obtain printed summary statistics or participant data before standardization; figures were not digitized.

The tables report posterior SDs and Bayesian compatibility intervals. Posterior SDs are retained literally in regression.model and in source quotes because the requested schema has no dedicated posterior-SD field. Do not treat regression.se=null as absence of Bayesian uncertainty, or convert these SDs into outcome SDs.
Table 3 gives a negative posterior SD for the GenAI total effect on Variety. The sign is preserved as printed; a valid posterior SD requires correction by the authors.

Several textual compatibility intervals differ from the corresponding table cells, and the direct Variety interval in the text is malformed. Structured values consistently use the tables. The conclusion also conflicts with the total-effect ordering of GenAI and Image Search for Fluency and Variety.

No numerical GenAI-versus-Image-Search contrast or its uncertainty is printed for any eligible outcome. Shared-baseline coefficients cannot supply its uncertainty, and no subtraction has been performed.

The screening form flags the actual Fluency model response and the normalization of Figure 8 as unresolved. The methods name sketch count for Fluency and clusters covered minus one for the Variety count model. No arm-level transformation, shifted sketch count, or graph-derived value is assumed here.

The paper does not specify how the design-fixation raters’ counts were combined for modelling, or print the model observation count. Output is the stated scoring unit, and participant random effects justify se_basis participant.
The study protocol is described as supplementary material but is not included in the saved PDF and has no printed retrieval URL. It might clarify allocation and scoring details.
The study country and Midjourney V4 release year are not stated. Author affiliations do not establish the study country, and the study date is not a model release year. Both fields remain null.
notes: Extracted by A on 2026-10-10. The full markdown conversion, including references and Appendix A, was read from start to end; every cited PDF page was checked with PyMuPDF.
